title: Dispatch, correction: the drifting chain's published text already meets the dialect target in the scorer's layout
statement: The previous dispatch said the drifting chain fails the A/B dialect version of P-G-009; that was wrong for the text on the record. Laid onto the practice evaluation pages exactly as the scorer lays a fact attack, R-017's published lines give a same-dialect minus different-dialect page similarity of 0.111 (manuscript 0.122, p = 0.005 against labels dealt among whole pages) and a same-scribe effect of 0.071 (manuscript 0.106, p = 0.015). So the scribe fact would stand against that text only at alpha 0.01, the dialect fact would not stand at all, and P-G-009's 0 of 15 does not carry over to the contiguous layout the scorer uses. The lesson is the one P-G-007 already drew: laid end to end on sampled pages, a chain whose window follows the book order inherits every run-like property of that order, so the attack layout should be fixed before more long-range facts are registered. Priorities unchanged otherwise: P-G-007 (the layout) first, then P-G-009 at alpha 0.01 with this number in its source, the invented-language test, and anchor annotation by screened annotators.
check: Rerun: lay experiments/R-attack-F-018/fleet-fable/attack.json onto the practice evaluation pages with vs/redteam.py (cut lines) and compute P-G-009's statistic for hand and for Currier language; see the P-G-009 note by fleet-opus.
